newsitem.title: ITALY: TENNIS-MARTINEZ ON COURSE FOR CLASH WITH SANCHEZ.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-MARTINEZ ON COURSE FOR CLASH WITH SANCHEZ.

text.p: Reigning champion Conchita Martinez stormed into the semifinals of the Italian Open women's tennis tournament on Friday with a no-nonsense defeat of unseeded South African Joannette Kruger.

The Spanish third seed, winner of the Foro Italico clay court tournament for a record four consecutive years, won 6-0 6-4 to stay on course for a semifinal clash with second-seeded compatriot Arantxa Sanchez Vicario.
Former world number one Sanchez was due to play unseeded Swiss Patty Schnyder in the late match under floodlights.
Martinez offered few frills in her demolition of Kruger. She turned up, performed the routine task demanded of her and then clocked off.
The only real emotion on a sun-baked centre court was the occasional scream from Kruger at yet another lost point.
Saturday will see Martinez's fifth successive semifinal at the Italian Open and her sixth in total.

The Spaniard's last defeat at the Foro Italico dates back to the 1991 semifinal when she lost to now-retired Argentine Gabriela Sabatini, who went on to take the title. She did not compete at the 1992 Open.
Austrian Barbara Paulus won through in the other half of the draw.

The 11th seed, who has not played in Rome since 1989, defeated Romanian seventh seed Irina Spirlea 6-4 6-2 and now meets either France's Mary Pierce, conqueror of top seed Monica Seles on Thursday, or Romanian Ruxandra Dragomir.
"They are both very good," said Paulus. "Dragomir was finalist at Hamburg last week while everyone knows that Mary Pierce plays a very powerful game."
Paulus was injured in 1990 and took three years off the circuit as she recovered and had treatment to her knees, ankles and wrists -- seven operations in all.
"I didn't expect too much but it is working," she said. "I think now I'm playing better than in 1990."
"I really didn't expect to reach the top 20 again," the 17th-ranked Austrian said.

Kruger captured just 12 points from Martinez in a lightning first set as the former Wimbledon champion, whose more interesting comments in a subsequent news conference concerned her love of motorbikes, revved up and roared away.
The second set was more of a contest and brought, momentarily, a vague hint of suspense.
Martinez broke Kruger in the opening game and then held serve before herself suffering a rare service break.
Kruger, a quarter-finalist in Rome in 1995, went 3-2 ahead before Martinez again broke her serve and went on to take the set 6-4, serving out to love.
"I think Rome is always special for me...I've always played well here, I don't know why," the Spaniard said.
